import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{post_heading}

Posted by: {user_name}

{post_content}
{post_tags}
""" def build_post_html(user_name: str, post_heading: str, post_content: str, post_tags: list[str]) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- user_name : str Author's name. post_heading : str Title of the post. post_content : str Main body of the post. post_tags : list[str] List of tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str A string containing a safe HTML snippet for rendering the post. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the required arguments are missing or empty. """ # Basic validation to avoid generating malformed HTML if not all([user_name, post_heading, post_content]) or post_tags is None: raise ValueError("All arguments must be provided and non-empty") # Escape user-provided data to prevent XSS esc_user_name = html.escape(user_name, quote=True) esc_post_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=True) esc_post_content = html.escape(post_content, quote=False) # Render each tag as a element and escape the tag text escaped_tags = [] for tag in post_tags: if not isinstance(tag, str): continue # skip non-string tags escaped_tag = html.escape(tag, quote=True) escaped_tags.append(f'{escaped_tag}') post_tags_html = ' '.join(escaped_tags) # Substitute placeholders in the template html_output = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( user_name=esc_user_name, post_heading=esc_post_heading, post_content=esc_post_content, post_tags=post_tags_html ) return html_output.strip()
